name: The Industrial Revolution
description: Steam engines, factories, railways and steel: how Britain and then the world moved from hand work to machines.

checkpoints.name: The first steam engines
checkpoints.note: Darby smelts iron with coke, Newcomen's engines pump water from mines, Kay's flying shuttle and Hargreaves' spinning jenny speed up cloth making, and canals carry coal to the towns.

checkpoints.name: Factories and iron
checkpoints.note: The Iron Bridge shows what cast iron can do, Adam Smith's Wealth of Nations explains the new economy, the Corn Laws of 1815 keep grain dear, and Stephenson's Rocket proves steam trains can work.

checkpoints.name: The railway age
checkpoints.note: The Liverpool and Manchester Railway opens, telegraph wires follow the lines, and Brunel builds tunnels and ships. Chartists march for the vote, Railway Mania ruins investors, Dickens writes of the poor, and Marx publishes The Communist Manifesto.

checkpoints.name: Steel and the telegraph
checkpoints.note: The Great Exhibition shows British industry to the world. The Bessemer process makes cheap steel, cables and the Suez Canal shrink distances, and the cholera outbreak of 1854 in Broad Street shows the cost of crowded cities.

checkpoints.name: The second industrial revolution
checkpoints.note: Steam turbines, electricity and steel take over from the first generation, and industry spreads to Germany, where Krupp grows into a giant, and to Japan, which began to industrialise after the Meiji Restoration.
